candidates.source_name: BQK — Lista e institucioneve financiare të licencuara/regjistruara (List of licensed/registered financial institutions, PDF series)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative periodically-updated roster naming every licensed payment institution, e-money institution, money-transfer NBFI and registered PSP in Kosovo — this is the definitive buyer universe for the non-bank payments cell; each new edition reveals newly licensed entrants who then procure switching, KYC and POS/agent infrastructure.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl of the bqk-kos.org uploads directory for new 'Lista-e-institucioneve-financiare-*' PDFs (ALB + ENG variants); diff entity lists between editions to detect new licences/withdrawals. Needs browser-like headers/session — plain fetch returned 403.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search (sq) for the BQK register of payment and e-money institutions
queries_used: BQK regjistri i institucioneve të pagesave dhe parasë elektronike
Kosovo payment institution licensed BQK register e-money
candidates.observed_blocker: WebFetch of the ALB PDF returned HTTP 403 Forbidden; the file is indexed and linked publicly, so this reads as bot-defence rather than removal — treat as live-but-unverified.

candidates.why_relevant: Defines the licensing gate that creates new payment-institution buyers and imposes obligations (outsourcing approval, security, agent registration) that translate directly into technology procurement. Regulation vintages signal upcoming compliance-driven spend waves.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Track the BQK 'korniza ligjore / rregulloret' section for new and amended PI/EMI regulations; snapshot each PDF with its board-approval date.

candidates.why_relevant: Agent networks are the physical distribution channel of Kosovo remittance and e-money firms; the agent regime governs registration of agent points and therefore the scale of agent-facing terminal, till and KYC tooling procurement.

candidates.why_relevant: The central bank is itself the operator of Kosovo's only payment system (IPS) and a contracting authority; its tender page is the single most direct public feed of payment-infrastructure procurement (switching, instant payments, cash/ATM handling, security) in the country.

candidates.source_name: e-Prokurimi — Kosovo national public e-procurement platform (Agjencia Qendrore e Prokurimit / KRPP)
candidates.why_relevant: Publicly-owned payment-adjacent buyers in this cell — Telekomi i Kosovës (Vala mobile payment arm), Posta e Kosovës/NPOSTA (postal payments and agent counters), KOSTT, municipalities buying cash-in/cash-out and card acceptance — are all bound by the Public Procurement Law and must publish contract and award notices here. It is the only mandatory-publication channel touching this cell.
candidates.legal_status: public by law (Ligji Nr. 04/L-042 për prokurimin publik)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword-watch notice titles in sq/sr/en for POS, terminale, kartela, pagesa elektronike, ATM/bankomat, switch, KYC; filter by the payment-adjacent contracting authorities above. Portal is dynamic — expect a session-based scraper rather than static fetch.

negative_findings.description: No public tender portal, notice board or RFP feed operated by any Kosovo licensed payment institution, e-money institution or remittance firm was found. Searched in sq ('tender', 'njoftim për kontratë', 'furnizim me terminale POS') and en against company sites (UFP, Moneta, OneFor, Swinto, IBAS, Paysera Kosova).
negative_findings.result_summary: Private payment-sector procurement in Kosovo appears to be entirely unpublished; only corporate news, partner press and job ads reveal it.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Coverage of this cell cannot rely on tender feeds — it must be built from the licence register plus company/partner/vendor announcement monitoring, which changes the collection design and expected latency.

negative_findings.description: No independent third-party card switch, processor or ATM/POS network operator serving Kosovo was identified. Searches in en and sq repeatedly returned only BQK (operator of the sole payment system, the Interbank Payment System) and individual banks' own acquiring.
negative_findings.result_summary: Switching/processing appears to be bank-internal or outsourced abroad rather than run by a domestic non-bank processor.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If confirmed, the 'processor' segment of this cell is empty domestically and terminal/switching demand sits with banks and with foreign processors — a materially different buyer map than assumed in the cell definition.

negative_findings.description: Two bqk-kos.org URLs (the licensed-institutions list PDF and the non-bank financial institutions section page) returned HTTP 403 on fetch, although both are indexed and linked from search results.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hypothesis: bot defence / user-agent filtering on the BQK web server, not removal.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most important register in this cell needs a browser-grade fetcher; a naive crawler would wrongly record it as dead.

negative_findings.description: Serbian-language (sr) searching produced no Kosovo-specific non-bank payments procurement sources. Cyrillic queries on Kosovo payment processing tenders returned only Serbia-domestic material (NBS tariffs, Serbian banks, KZK case files).
negative_findings.result_summary: sr coverage of this cell is effectively empty at the search-engine level; north-Kosovo payment arrangements were not surfaced by these queries.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The Serbian-language segment of Kosovo's payments landscape (Serbian-system institutions and cash/remittance channels in the north) may be systematically invisible to this method and needs a targeted approach.

negative_findings.description: Several fintechs surfaced (IBAS, Swinto, UPay) describe themselves as licensed e-money or payment platforms serving Kosovo, but their licensing jurisdiction was not confirmed against the BQK register within this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: Names captured as candidates with reduced credibility scores pending register cross-check.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Treating an EU-licensed firm as a BQK licensee would distort the buyer universe for this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: The BQK register PDF could not be parsed in this run, so the authoritative enumeration of licensed PIs, EMIs and money-transfer NBFIs (beyond UFP, Moneta and the fintechs found via press) is still incomplete.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch the latest 'Lista e institucioneve financiare' PDF with a browser-grade client, extract the non-bank sections, and make that list the spine of the cell's actor map.

coverage_gaps.description: Mobile operators' payment arms (Telekomi i Kosovës/Vala, IPKO) were only partially covered — IPKO, being privately owned, publishes no procurement and was not reached by these queries.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Profile IPKO (Telekom Slovenije group) via group-level supplier announcements, ARKEP regulatory filings and job ads; add ARKEP as a telecom-regulator pointer source.

coverage_gaps.description: No sr-language sources for this cell were found; north-Kosovo payment/remittance arrangements are unrepresented.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run targeted sr queries against Kosovo-north media (Kossev, Radio KIM) and Serbian institutions with Kosovo operations, using terms like 'платни промет', 'мењачница', 'дознаке', 'Косово и Метохија'.

coverage_gaps.description: Because private payment firms do not tender publicly, contract intelligence for this cell must come from vendor-side disclosure, which was not systematically searched.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a vendor-side sweep: press rooms and customer-reference pages of terminal/switch/KYC suppliers active in the Balkans, plus Kosovo job postings naming specific payment platforms, as the primary indirect evidence of contracts.

coverage_gaps.description: e-Prokurimi was identified but its search interface, filters and export behaviour were not exercised, so it is unknown whether payment-keyword monitoring can be automated or needs an account.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Do a dedicated feasibility pass on e-prokurimi.rks-gov.net: test notice search by keyword and contracting authority, and check whether KRPP publishes bulk annual contract datasets.

brief: Kosovo's non-bank payments buyer universe is defined almost entirely by one regulator artefact — the BQK 'Lista e institucioneve financiare të licencuara/regjistruara' plus the PI/EMI authorisation and agent regulations — while the buyers themselves (Unioni Financiar Prishtinë as Western Union agent, Moneta as MoneyGram agent, and a newer wallet/e-money cohort including OneFor, Swinto, IBAS and Paysera Kosova) publish no tenders at all. The only mandatory-publication procurement channel touching this cell is the state e-Prokurimi portal, via publicly-owned payment-adjacent buyers (Telekomi i Kosovës/Vala, Posta e Kosovës) and the central bank's own tender page, supplemented by IFI/donor procurement such as the World Bank's electronic payment acceptance work. Contract intelligence therefore has to be assembled indirectly — from Kosovo investigative media that expose negotiated-without-publication awards, from BQK card/POS statistics that size the terminal estate, and from ARBK entity records — rather than from any payments-industry tender feed. Two structural weaknesses stand out: no domestic non-bank card switch or ATM/POS network operator could be evidenced, and Serbian-language coverage of this cell is currently empty.
